# Data format

<!-- generated by `python -m dayring schema --markdown`; edit dayring/schema.py instead -->

All tables are UTF-8 CSV files with a header row, kept in the data directory
named in ``dayring.toml``. Importers write them; modules only read them.
``docs/DATA_FORMAT.md`` is generated from this file (``python -m dayring schema --markdown``).

Conventions
- ``date``: local calendar day, ``YYYY-MM-DD``.
- ``datetime``: local wall-clock time without offset, ``YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM`` (seconds optional).
  The timezone is the one in ``dayring.toml``. One exception: ``sleep_start`` / ``sleep_end`` from
  Apple Health are in the zone you slept in, so a night abroad reads as you lived it.
- Minutes are real minutes: on the day clocks go forward the skipped hour is not counted, and a
  record that runs through the repeated hour when they go back counts it twice (23- and 25-hour days).
- Empty cell = unknown. Unknown is never read as zero.
- A sleep belongs to the day you woke up.

## `body_daily.csv`

One row per day of body measurements, usually from a watch or phone.

Key: `date`. Typical sources: Apple Health export (dayring import apple-health); any CSV with these columns.

| column | type | required | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `date` | date | yes | The day. Sleep is filed under the day you woke up. |
| `sleep_min` | number |  | Minutes asleep in the main sleep that ended this day. |
| `in_bed_min` | number |  | Minutes in bed for the same sleep. |
| `sleep_start` | datetime |  | When you fell asleep (local time). |
| `sleep_end` | datetime |  | When you woke up (local time). |
| `hrv_ms` | number |  | Heart-rate variability (SDNN or RMSSD, but keep one kind), ms. |
| `resting_hr` | number |  | Resting heart rate, beats per minute. |
| `steps` | number |  | Steps that day. |
| `exercise_min` | number |  | Minutes of exercise (Apple 'Exercise' ring or similar). |
| `workout_min` | number |  | Minutes of logged workouts. 0 means rest day; empty means unknown. |
| `workout_type` | text |  | Main workout that day, free text (e.g. strength, run). |
| `weight_kg` | number |  | Body weight, kg. |
| `waist_cm` | number |  | Waist, cm. |
| `complete` | flag |  | 1 if the day was over when the data was exported; 0 if the export happened mid-day (then steps and minutes are not compared with your normal). |

## `workouts.csv`

Each workout with its start and end, e.g. from Apple Fitness or a watch. The Time page uses the times; body_daily.workout_min is the daily total. A workout paused along the way can be one row per stretch of moving (the Apple Health importer writes it so), so the minutes are the time spent moving. `end` must be after `start`.

Key: `start`, `type`. Typical sources: Apple Health export, which includes Apple Fitness and Workout app sessions (dayring import apple-health); Strava, Garmin or any CSV with these columns.

| column | type | required | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `start` | datetime | yes | Start (local time). |
| `end` | datetime | yes | End (local time). |
| `type` | text | yes | What kind of workout, e.g. strength training, running. |
| `source` | text |  | Which app or device recorded it. |
| `kcal` | number |  | Active energy for the workout, kcal. |

## `self_report.csv`

How you said you felt, on a 0–5 scale. Optional; pages show a prompt when it is empty.

Key: `date`. Typical sources: typed by hand; an assistant that writes this file for you.

| column | type | required | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `date` | date | yes | The day. |
| `energy` | number |  | Body energy, 0 (drained) to 5 (full). |
| `focus` | number |  | Mental focus, 0 to 5. |
| `note` | text |  | One line in your own words. |

## `screen_sessions.csv`

Foreground app sessions across your devices. Overlaps between devices are allowed; dayring counts wall-clock time once, preferring the device order in dayring.toml (the Time page's devices-at-once card counts each device on its own). `end` must be after `start`.

Key: `start`, `device`, `app`. Typical sources: macOS Screen Time / Biome (dayring import macos-screentime); RescueTime or ActivityWatch CSV; any CSV with these columns.

| column | type | required | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `start` | datetime | yes | Session start (local time). |
| `end` | datetime | yes | Session end (local time). |
| `device` | text | yes | Device name, e.g. laptop, phone, tablet. |
| `app` | text | yes | App name or website domain. |
| `category` | text | yes | What kind of use it was. One of: `work`, `learning`, `communication`, `entertainment`, `social`, `other`. |

## `events.csv`

Calendar blocks: classes, work shifts, planned training.

Key: `start`, `title`. Typical sources: any .ics calendar (dayring import ics); any CSV with these columns.

| column | type | required | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `start` | datetime | yes | Start (local time). |
| `end` | datetime | yes | End (local time). |
| `title` | text | yes | What it is. |
| `kind` | text | yes | Type of block. One of: `class`, `work`, `training`, `personal`, `other`. |
| `location` | text |  | Where. |

## `deadlines.csv`

Things due on a date: assignments, exams, milestones.

Key: `due`, `title`. Typical sources: typed by hand; a course or project tracker export.

| column | type | required | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `due` | datetime | yes | When it is due (local time). Use 23:59 if only the day is known. |
| `title` | text | yes | What is due. |
| `group` | text |  | Course or project it belongs to. |
| `weight_pct` | number |  | Share of the course grade, percent. Empty if it is not graded. |
| `status` | text |  | Where it stands. One of: `todo`, `submitted`, `done`. |
| `note` | text |  | Format, length, group size, anything you want to see next to it. |

## `ai_work.csv`

Stretches when an AI coding agent was working for you: model calls of one session no more than 5 minutes apart. Several sessions at once each count, like several people working. Only times, counts and model token totals; never what was said. A tool busy for over 5 minutes between two calls is missed, so it is a lower bound.

Key: `start`, `tool`, `session`. Typical sources: Claude Code and Codex logs on this computer (dayring import ai-logs); any CSV with these columns.

| column | type | required | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `start` | datetime | yes | First call of the stretch (local time, rounded down to the minute). |
| `end` | datetime | yes | Last call of the stretch (local time, rounded up to the minute). |
| `tool` | text | yes | Which agent. One of: `claude_code`, `codex`, `other`. |
| `session` | text | yes | A short code for the session (a hash, never the tool's own id). |
| `started_by` | text | yes | Who started the session: you, a scheduled task or a script (claude -p, codex exec). Only yours count as your AI work. One of: `you`, `scheduled`, `script`. |
| `minutes` | number | yes | Minutes of work inside the stretch (exact; start and end are rounded). |
| `calls` | number |  | Model calls in the stretch. |
| `output_tokens` | number |  | Tokens the model wrote in the stretch. |

## `ai_prompts.csv`

The instructions you typed to an AI coding agent, counted per minute. Only the time; never the text.

Key: `time`, `tool`, `session`. Typical sources: Claude Code and Codex logs on this computer (dayring import ai-logs); any CSV with these columns.

| column | type | required | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `time` | datetime | yes | The minute (local time). |
| `tool` | text | yes | Which agent. One of: `claude_code`, `codex`, `other`. |
| `session` | text | yes | A short code for the session (a hash, never the tool's own id). |
| `started_by` | text | yes | Who started the session. One of: `you`, `scheduled`, `script`. |
| `count` | number | yes | Instructions in that minute. |
